Key Research Thinking Patterns: Digital Twin-Integrated Security Validation: Leveraging digital twin environments to simulate and detect adversarial behaviors in distributed systems, enabling proactive mitigation of threats like data poisoning in Federated Learning. (e.g., DT-FU framework using Digital Twins to autonomously identify malicious clients and validate unlearning efficacy via backdoor accuracy reduction metrics.)

Gradient-Based Selective Unlearning: Employing mathematical optimization techniques, specifically gradient ascent, to selectively erase the influence of compromised data or clients from global models without requiring full retraining. (e.g., UaaS-SFL framework utilizing gradient ascent and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) to restore model integrity post-poisoning with <10% accuracy deviation.)

Adversarial Perturbation for Source-Level Privacy: Generating maximally perturbed yet semantically consistent data at the source to ensure sensitive information (e.g., biometric data) never leaves local devices, balancing privacy with utility. (e.g., AML-FL framework using noise generators to create adversarial examples that maintain 96.24% accuracy in distributed settings while preserving local data privacy.)

Hybrid Optimization for Heterogeneous Network Control: Combining game-theoretic strategies for resource allocation with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and evolutionary algorithms to optimize complex, multi-agent physical network parameters. (e.g., 6G HAP-UAV-RIS framework using Game Theory for task offloading, PPO for UAV trajectory, and Differential Evolution for RIS phase shift optimization to maximize energy efficiency and coverage.)
Summary Description: Mohammad Atiquzzaman is a principal investigator specializing in the security, privacy, and resilience of next-generation 6G networks and distributed AI systems. His research focuses on integrating Federated Learning (FL) with Digital Twin (DT) technologies to create secure, privacy-preserving infrastructure for smart cities and vehicular networks. Key methodological contributions include the development of 'Unlearning as a Service' (UaaS-SFL) frameworks that use gradient ascent to mitigate data poisoning attacks without full retraining, and adversarial machine learning techniques for source-level data privacy in biometric surveillance. Additionally, he designs energy-efficient aerial network architectures using Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) and UAVs, employing hybrid optimization strategies (Game Theory, DRL, and evolutionary algorithms) to enhance disaster response capabilities and urban monitoring reliability. His work bridges the gap between theoretical security mechanisms and practical deployment in IoT, MEC, and autonomous systems.
